examples.name: FileInput
examples.code:
<FileInput
  name="file"
  onChange={event => {
    const fileList = event.target.files;
    for (let i = 0; i < fileList.length; i += 1) {
      const file = fileList[i];
    }
  }}
/>

prose.title: React/DOM Properties
prose.text:
At its core, the FileInput component is a regular <input> element. Thus, both DOM and React properties, methods, and events are accessible. To read up on all of the possible DOM attributes and types available for input elements, check out this [MDN Web Documents page.](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input) To learn more about DOM events and methods, you can read more on the [MDN Web Events documentation page](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Events).

Also, feel free to read about the [types of React events available](https://reactjs.org/docs/handling-events.html), or see [how DOM attributes change in React.](https://reactjs.org/docs/dom-elements.html) Working in tandem with Styled Components, you also have access to the [as property.](https://styled-components.com/docs/api#as-polymorphic-prop)

tables.name: Props
rows: Provides custom rendering of a confirmation that appears when the user attempts to remove a file or files.
The function will be passed an object containing 'onConfirm' and 'onCancel' callbacks. If 'onConfirm' is called, the file will be removed. If 'onCancel' is called, the file will remain.

({ onConfirm, onCancel }) => (
  <Layer onClickOutside={onCancel} onEsc={onCancel}>
      <Box>
          Are you sure you want to delete this file?
          <Box direction="row" gap="small">
             <Button label="Cancel" onClick={onCancel} />
             <Button label="Delete file" onClick={onConfirm} />
          </Box>
      </Box>
  </Layer>
)
The id attribute of the input.
Specifies a file size limit in bytes (binary) for FileInput.
Custom messages for FileInput. Used for internationalization and customization of default strings and accessibility announcements. readers.

If an object is supplied, 'aggregageThreshold' indicates the maximum number of individual files to show. Above this, only a single message describing the number of files will be shown. 'max' indicates the maximum number of files that can be added.
The name attribute of the input. This is required when used within a Form.
Function that will be called when one or more files are added to or removed from the input.

The function will be passed two arguments: the event
            and an object with key 'files'. The file(s) can be found in
            event.target.files or by deconstructing files from the second
            argument. For example: (event, {files}) => {}.
Provides custom rendering of the file. If not provided, the file's name will be shown.
The function will be passed the browser File object as an argument.
